requirements.subject: ent:parameterized-object
requirements.canonical: A module, structured type, template, function, altstep or testcase MAY be defined incompletely, i.e. with entities (variables, templates, ports, timers, etc.) used in its definition left unresolved.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 modules, structured types, templates, functions, altsteps, and testcases may be defined incompletely, i.e. some entities (variables, templates, ports, timers, etc.) used by the above objects may not be resolved in the definition of the object.

ambiguity.issue: Structured types are listed as parameterizable, but table 2 lists only module, template, function, altstep and testcase, and clause 5.4.1.1 restriction a) forbids parameterization of record of, set of and enumerated definitions. Chosen reading: the list is as stated, the table and restrictions determine which kinds are actually parameterizable.
readings: A module, structured type, template, function, altstep or testcase MAY be parameterized.
Only a module, template, function, altstep or testcase MAY be parameterized; structured types are not parameterizable.

requirements.subject: ent:parameterized-object
requirements.canonical: A module, structured type, template, function, altstep or testcase defined with unresolved entities IS called a parameterized object.
requirements.original: These objects are called parameterized objects.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal entity replacing an unresolved entity in the definition of a parameterized object IS called a formal parameter.
requirements.original: Formal entities replacing the unresolved entities in the parameterized object's definition are called formal parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter of a parameterized template, function, altstep or testcase IS defined in a formal parameter list.
requirements.original: Formal parameters of parameterized templates, functions, altsteps, and testcases are defined in formal parameter lists.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter of a module IS defined in a module parameter definition.
requirements.original: Formal parameters of modules are defined in module parameter definitions (see clause 8.2.1).

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter SHALL be an in, inout or out parameter.
requirements.original: Formal parameters shall be in, inout or out parameters (see terms in clause 3.1).

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: If not stated otherwise, a formal parameter IS an in parameter.
requirements.original: If not stated otherwise, a formal parameter is an in parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter, whether in, inout or out, CAN be both read and set within the parameterized object.
requirements.original: For all these three sorts of parameter passing, the formal parameters can both be read and set (i.e. get new values being assigned) within the parameterized object.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter MAY be used directly as an actual parameter of another parameterized object, e.g. in a function invocation or in a template instance.
requirements.original: Formal parameters can be used directly as actual parameters for other parameterized objects, e.g. as actual parameters in function invocations or as actual parameters in template instances.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the parameter is passed by value
requirements.canonical: If a parameter is passed by value (in and out parameters), the type compatibility rules of clause 6.3 SHALL apply between the actual parameter and the formal parameter.
requirements.original: If parameters are passed by value (i.e. in case of in and out parameters), type compatibility rules specified in clause 6.3 apply.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the parameter is passed by reference
requirements.canonical: If a parameter is passed by reference, strong typing SHALL be applied between the actual parameter and the formal parameter.
requirements.original: When parameters are passed by reference, strong typing is required.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the parameter is passed by reference
requirements.canonical: If a parameter is passed by reference, the actual parameter SHALL be of the same type as the formal parameter.
requirements.original: Both the actual and formal parameter shall be of the same type.

requirements.subject: ent:in-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal in parameter MAY have a default value.
requirements.original: Formal in parameters may have default values.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: If no actual parameter is provided for a formal in parameter with a default value, the default value IS used as the value of the formal parameter.
requirements.original: This default value is used when no actual parameter is provided.

requirements.subject: ent:out-parameter
requirements.canonical: An out formal parameter CAN be read within the parameterized object, but it does not inherit the value of its actual parameter.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Although out parameters can be read within the parameterized object, they do not inherit the value of their actual parameter; i.e. they should be set before they are read.

requirements.subject: ent:out-parameter
requirements.canonical: An out formal parameter SHOULD be set before it is read within the parameterized object.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Although out parameters can be read within the parameterized object, they do not inherit the value of their actual parameter; i.e. they should be set before they are read.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter or formal template parameter MAY be declared lazy using the `@lazy` modifier.
requirements.original: Formal value or template parameters may be declared lazy using the @lazy modifier.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-parameter
requirements.canonical: A lazy formal parameter IS evaluated as specified by the definition of lazy values or templates in clause 3.1.
requirements.original: The behaviour of lazy parameters is defined in clause 3.1, definition of lazy values or templates.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter or formal template parameter MAY be declared fuzzy using the `@fuzzy` modifier.
requirements.original: Formal value or template parameters may be declared fuzzy using the @fuzzy modifier.

requirements.subject: ent:fuzzy-parameter
requirements.canonical: A fuzzy formal parameter IS evaluated as specified by the definition of fuzzy values or templates in clause 3.1.
requirements.original: The behaviour of fuzzy parameters is defined in clause 3.1, definition of fuzzy values or templates.

requirements.subject: ent:deterministic-modifier
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter or formal template parameter declared lazy or fuzzy MAY additionally be declared deterministic using the `@deterministic` modifier.
requirements.original: Formal value or template parameters that are declared lazy or fuzzy can be additionally declared deterministic using the @deterministic modifier.

requirements.subject: ent:component-variable
requirements.canonical: The value of a component variable used in the delayed evaluation of a lazy or fuzzy parameter CAN differ from its value at the time the parameterized function or altstep was called.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The actual values of component variables used in the delayed evaluation of a lazy or fuzzy parameter may differ from their values at the time, when the parameterized function or altstep was called.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: Assigning a default value to a lazy or fuzzy formal parameter does NOT change the semantics of the parameter.
requirements.original: Assigning default values for lazy and fuzzy formal parameters does not change the parameters' semantics: when the default values are used as actual values for the parameters, they shall be evaluated the same way (i.e. delayed) as if an actual parameter was provided.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.condition: the default value of a lazy or fuzzy formal parameter is used
requirements.canonical: When the default value of a lazy or fuzzy formal parameter is used as the actual value, it SHALL be evaluated in the same delayed way as if an actual parameter was provided.
requirements.original: Assigning default values for lazy and fuzzy formal parameters does not change the parameters' semantics: when the default values are used as actual values for the parameters, they shall be evaluated the same way (i.e. delayed) as if an actual parameter was provided.

requirements.subject: ent:module
requirements.canonical: A module SHALL support value parameterization only.
requirements.original: Keyword: module; Allowed kind of Parameterization: Value parameterization; Allowed form of Parameterization: Static at start of runtime; Allowed types in formal parameter lists: all basic types, all user-defined types and address type.

requirements.subject: ent:module
requirements.canonical: The parameterization of a module IS static at start of runtime.
requirements.original: Keyword: module; Allowed kind of Parameterization: Value parameterization; Allowed form of Parameterization: Static at start of runtime; Allowed types in formal parameter lists: all basic types, all user-defined types and address type.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: A module parameter MAY be of any basic type, any user-defined type or the address type.
requirements.original: Keyword: module; Allowed kind of Parameterization: Value parameterization; Allowed form of Parameterization: Static at start of runtime; Allowed types in formal parameter lists: all basic types, all user-defined types and address type.

ambiguity.issue: Table 2 speaks of 'formal parameter lists' for modules, but module parameters are defined in module parameter definitions, not in a formal parameter list.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A `template` definition MAY have value parameterization and template parameterization.
requirements.original: Keyword: template; Allowed kind of Parameterization: Value and template parameterization; Allowed form of Parameterization: Dynamic at runtime; Allowed types in formal parameter lists: all basic types, all user-defined types, address type and template.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: The parameterization of a `template` IS dynamic at runtime.
requirements.original: Keyword: template; Allowed kind of Parameterization: Value and template parameterization; Allowed form of Parameterization: Dynamic at runtime; Allowed types in formal parameter lists: all basic types, all user-defined types, address type and template.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter-list
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter in the formal parameter list of a `template` MAY be of any basic type, any user-defined type, the address type, or be a template parameter.
requirements.original: Keyword: template; Allowed kind of Parameterization: Value and template parameterization; Allowed form of Parameterization: Dynamic at runtime; Allowed types in formal parameter lists: all basic types, all user-defined types, address type and template.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A `function` definition MAY have value parameterization and template parameterization.
requirements.original: Keyword: function; Allowed kind of Parameterization: Value and template parameterization; Allowed form of Parameterization: Dynamic at runtime; Allowed types in formal parameter lists: all basic types, all user-defined types, address type, component type, port type, default, template and timer.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: The parameterization of a `function` IS dynamic at runtime.
requirements.original: Keyword: function; Allowed kind of Parameterization: Value and template parameterization; Allowed form of Parameterization: Dynamic at runtime; Allowed types in formal parameter lists: all basic types, all user-defined types, address type, component type, port type, default, template and timer.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter-list
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter in the formal parameter list of a `function` MAY be of any basic type, any user-defined type, the address type, a component type, a port type, the default type or the timer type, or be a template parameter.
requirements.original: Keyword: function; Allowed kind of Parameterization: Value and template parameterization; Allowed form of Parameterization: Dynamic at runtime; Allowed types in formal parameter lists: all basic types, all user-defined types, address type, component type, port type, default, template and timer.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: A `altstep` definition MAY have value parameterization and template parameterization.
requirements.original: Keyword: altstep; Allowed kind of Parameterization: Value and template parameterization; Allowed form of Parameterization: Dynamic at runtime; Allowed types in formal parameter lists: all basic types, all user-defined types, address type, component type, port type, default, template and timer.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: The parameterization of a `altstep` IS dynamic at runtime.
requirements.original: Keyword: altstep; Allowed kind of Parameterization: Value and template parameterization; Allowed form of Parameterization: Dynamic at runtime; Allowed types in formal parameter lists: all basic types, all user-defined types, address type, component type, port type, default, template and timer.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter-list
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter in the formal parameter list of a `altstep` MAY be of any basic type, any user-defined type, the address type, a component type, a port type, the default type or the timer type, or be a template parameter.
requirements.original: Keyword: altstep; Allowed kind of Parameterization: Value and template parameterization; Allowed form of Parameterization: Dynamic at runtime; Allowed types in formal parameter lists: all basic types, all user-defined types, address type, component type, port type, default, template and timer.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A `testcase` definition MAY have value parameterization and template parameterization.
requirements.original: Keyword: testcase; Allowed kind of Parameterization: Value and template parameterization; Allowed form of Parameterization: Dynamic at runtime; Allowed types in formal parameter lists: all basic types and of all user-defined types, address type, component type and template.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: The parameterization of a `testcase` IS dynamic at runtime.
requirements.original: Keyword: testcase; Allowed kind of Parameterization: Value and template parameterization; Allowed form of Parameterization: Dynamic at runtime; Allowed types in formal parameter lists: all basic types and of all user-defined types, address type, component type and template.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter-list
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter in the formal parameter list of a `testcase` MAY be of any basic type, any user-defined type, the address type or a component type, or be a template parameter.
requirements.original: Keyword: testcase; Allowed kind of Parameterization: Value and template parameterization; Allowed form of Parameterization: Dynamic at runtime; Allowed types in formal parameter lists: all basic types and of all user-defined types, address type, component type and template.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter of a `testcase` SHALL NOT be of a port type, the default type or the timer type.
requirements.original: Keyword: testcase; Allowed kind of Parameterization: Value and template parameterization; Allowed form of Parameterization: Dynamic at runtime; Allowed types in formal parameter lists: all basic types and of all user-defined types, address type, component type and template.

ambiguity.issue: Table 2 lists the allowed types for testcases without port, default and timer; the prohibition is implied by omission. Chosen reading: omission means prohibition (consistent with clause 5.4.1.1 restriction l).
readings: A formal parameter of a testcase SHALL NOT be of a port, default or timer type.
Table 2 is not exhaustive; other types may be allowed for testcase formal parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:signature
requirements.canonical: A signature IS not listed in table 2 because a signature declares parameters only.
requirements.original: NOTE: Signatures are not shown in the table, because a signature declares parameters only.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A template of a signature CAN be parameterized.
requirements.original: The templates for the signatures can be parameterized, however.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-parameter
requirements.canonical: The lazy or fuzzy property of a formal parameter IS valid only in the scope where the name of the parameter is visible.
requirements.original: Lazy and fuzzy properties are valid only in the scope, where the parameters' names are visible.

requirements.subject: ent:fuzzy-parameter
requirements.condition: a fuzzy parameter is passed to a formal parameter declared without `@lazy` or `@fuzzy`
requirements.canonical: If a fuzzy formal parameter is passed as actual parameter to a formal parameter declared without a modifier, the parameter IS NOT fuzzy inside the called function.
requirements.original: For example, if a fuzzy parameter is passed to a formal parameter declared without a modifier, it loses its fuzzy feature inside the called function.

requirements.subject: ent:fuzzy-parameter
requirements.condition: a fuzzy parameter is passed to a formal parameter declared `@lazy`
requirements.canonical: If a fuzzy formal parameter is passed as actual parameter to a lazy formal parameter, the parameter IS lazy inside the called function.
requirements.original: Similarly, if it is passed to a lazy formal parameter, it becomes lazy within the called function.

ambiguity.issue: 'it' (via 'Similarly') most likely refers to the fuzzy parameter of the preceding sentence; it could also be read as applying to any parameter passed on to a lazy formal parameter.
readings: A fuzzy formal parameter passed to a lazy formal parameter IS lazy within the called function.
Any formal parameter (lazy, fuzzy or without modifier) passed to a lazy formal parameter IS lazy within the called function.

non_requirement.reason: header row of table 2 (overview of parameterizable TTCN-3 objects)
